answer: In an AI-agent market serving lagoon farms, an agent buying trellis parts earns voting weight only by locking tokens for 90 days, with one vote per locked token. The protocol treats bonded capital as its signal of commitment and counts each token once, so splitting a stake among a thousand fake identities adds no influence. To gain more votes, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital, sacrificing liquidity and its use elsewhere.
